html:
The Madija, better known as the Kulina, are an Arawan-speaking people of the upper Juruá and Purus river basins in the western Amazon, in the Brazilian states of Acre and Amazonas and across the border in Peru. They should not be confused with the Panoan Kulina Pano.

They live in villages along the rivers, farming manioc, fishing and hunting. The rubber boom of the late 1800s drew rubber tappers up their rivers, bringing violence and disease. Their Arawan relatives include the Deni and the Jamamadi. With about 4,000 speakers, their language is considered threatened.
